questions.q: What does the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) under Basel III require banks to do?
options: Hold enough high-quality liquid assets to survive a 30-day acute stress scenario
Report quarterly earnings to the SEC
Fund all assets exclusively with short-term borrowing
Eliminate proprietary trading entirely
questions.explain: The LCR requires banks to hold sufficient high-quality liquid assets to survive a 30-day stress scenario, directly targeting funding liquidity risk.

questions.q: Why does Basel III require capital to be held against risk-weighted assets rather than total assets?
options: Because risk-weighting is simpler to calculate than total asset value
So that riskier assets require proportionally more capital backing than safer ones
Because regulators only care about a bank's cash holdings
Risk-weighting was eliminated from Basel III in its final version
questions.explain: Risk-weighted capital ratios scale required capital to the riskiness of the assets held, so a bank holding riskier assets must hold more capital than one holding safer assets of the same total value.

questions.q: Which two elements of the Dodd-Frank Act are specifically named in this lesson?
options: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio and the Net Stable Funding Ratio
Mandatory central clearing for many derivatives and the Volcker Rule
The CCAR and DFAST stress-testing programs
Probability of Default and Loss Given Default
questions.explain: Dodd-Frank introduced mandatory central clearing for many standardized derivatives and the Volcker Rule, which restricts certain bank proprietary trading.

questions.q: In the 'three lines of defense' risk governance model, what is the role of the second line?
options: Taking on risk directly through trading or business activity
Acting as an independent risk and compliance function that sets and monitors limits
Verifying, after the fact, that the first two lines are functioning as designed
Approving the firm's annual budget
questions.explain: The second line is an independent risk and compliance function sitting apart from the business line, responsible for setting limits and monitoring whether they are being respected. Internal audit, the third line, verifies the first two.

questions.q: Which US regulator is most associated with bank holding company oversight and systemic risk stress tests like CCAR/DFAST?
options: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
The Federal Reserve
The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)
questions.explain: The Federal Reserve oversees bank holding companies and systemic risk in the US, including running the CCAR and DFAST stress-testing programs introduced in Lesson 24.
